original_question: Let X be a metrizable space. If, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable, must X itself be completely metrizable?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Question 3.10: the open problem asking whether, for a metrizable space X, the requirement that every compatible metric yield a Wijsman hyperspace that is strongly Choquet or strongly α-favorable forces X to be completely metrizable. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost exactly: it has the right ambient class (metrizable spaces), the right universal quantifier over compatible metrics, the right hyperspace topology (Wijsman), the right game-theoretic properties (strongly Choquet / strongly α-favorable), and the right conclusion (complete metrizability of X). It matches the scope and logical form of Section 3, Question 3.10. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
missing_details: The paper uses 2^X to mean the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X; that should be stated explicitly if the question is to stand alone. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

T_W(d) should be identified as the Wijsman topology induced by d, i.e. the topology on 2^X coming from pointwise convergence of the distance functionals A ↦ d(x,A) for x in X. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

The game-theoretic terms are defined in the paper via the strong Choquet game: 'strongly α-favorable' means player α has a winning tactic, while 'strongly Choquet' means player α has a winning strategy. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

The conclusion should be understood topologically: 'X is completely metrizable' means that X admits some compatible complete metric, not that every compatible metric on X is complete. This is the meaning used in Theorem 3.5(3) and Question 3.10. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

For full paper-faithful context, the question is posed after Theorem 3.5, which proves the equivalence in the locally separable metrizable case, and after Theorem 3.6 plus Examples 3.7 and 3.8, which explain why weaker α-favorability statements do not settle the general problem. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
refined_question: Let X be a metrizable space, and let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X. For each metric d compatible with the topology of X, let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, namely the topology of pointwise convergence of the distance maps A ↦ d(x,A) for x ∈ X. If, for every compatible metric d on X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is either strongly Choquet or strongly α-favorable in the strong Choquet game, does it follow that X is completely metrizable, i.e. that X admits a compatible complete metric?
justification: The draft is not aiming at the broader Problem 3.1, but at the more specific open question extracted from that discussion. Section 3 first asks whether complete metrizability can be characterized by any completeness-type property of the Wijsman hyperspace; it then introduces game-theoretic completeness notions, proves in Theorem 3.5 that for locally separable metrizable spaces complete metrizability is equivalent to the 'for every compatible metric' strong α-favorability and strong Choquet conditions, and then immediately states the general converse question as Question 3.10. That is the nearest official formulation to your draft. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
